---
title: "Simulation (paper), step 2.1: generate pathologist counts and truths"
---

Step 2.1 of the paper simulation (pathologist design): for the datasets of step 1 with 40 slides
(scenarios A-C, replicates 1–100) and every pathologist variant, the slide and rater effects and the
detection counts (TP, FN, FP) of every rater on every slide, and the true values of recall,
precision and F1 for the average pathologist and for single pathologists.

**Data-generating process** (`simulate_rater_dataset()`)

- Slide effects on logit recall and log FP_rate, shared by all raters of a slide.
- Rater effects from two independent parts: skill s ~ N(0, σ_skill) (better on both) and cutoff
  c ~ N(0, σ_cutoff) (more liberal: higher recall, more FP).
  Effect on logit recall = s + c, effect on log FP_rate = g · (c − s).
- Every rater scores every slide: TP ~ Bin(P, recall_cell), FN = P − TP,
  FP ~ Poisson(FP_rate_cell + fp_per_object · P). No rater × slide effect.
- New raters for every dataset (the rater population is part of the estimand).

**Variants**

| Variant | Raters | recall | FP_rate | fp_per_object | σ_skill | σ_cutoff | g | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 data example | 23 | 0.63 | 4.2 | 0.015 | 0.20 | 0.55 | 2.0 | fit to the real pathologist data (σ_skill / σ_cutoff reduced from 0.15 / 0.57 for faster fitting) |
| 2 skilled panel | 9 | 0.70 | 3.0 | 0.015 | 0.55 | 0.20 | 2.0 | smaller panel, raters differ mainly in skill, better performance |

Both variants: slide SD 0.66 (logit recall) and 0.95 (log FP_rate), no slide correlation.
recall and FP_rate refer to the median rater on a slide with all effects = 0. Swapping σ_skill and
σ_cutoff keeps the SD of the rater effects (0.585 on logit recall, 1.17 on log FP_rate) and flips
their correlation from +0.77 (trade-off between recall and FP) to −0.77 (good raters better on both).

**Truths** (marginal, from expected counts per cell = slide × rater, E[TP] = P · recall_cell,
E[FP] = FP_rate_cell + fp_per_object · P, so there is no 0/0; formulas as `calc_true_metrics()` in
step 2)

- pooled: metric of the summed expected counts (Recall = Σ E[TP] / Σ P, Precision =
  Σ E[TP] / Σ (E[TP] + E[FP]), F1 = 2 Σ E[TP] / Σ (P + E[TP] + E[FP])).
- grouped: mean of the per-cell metrics (each cell same weight).
- Cells: 20,000 new raters from the rater distribution × the first 10,000 slides of the slide
  superpopulation of step 1, with own slide effects per variant. Computed one scenario and variant
  at a time and reduced to one row per rater (sums of the expected counts, per-rater grouped values).
- **Average pathologist:** over all cells (pathologists and slides), i.e. the population value of the
  rater population (not the rater with effects = 0). The raters with many FP dominate the pooled
  sums (FP_rate is lognormal over the raters), hence the 20,000 raters: Monte Carlo SE at most 0.003
  for pooled and 0.0015 for grouped (bootstrap over the raters in the check; peak memory about 34 GB).
- **Single pathologist:** per new rater over the slides (20,000 values per scenario and variant; truth
  for the "single pathologist" prediction interval). Same raters and slides as the average
  pathologist.

**Seeds** (own offset, no collision with the offsets of `01_seed_offsets.csv`)

- Counts of a dataset: `seed + 10000000 * variant`.
- Slide effects of the superpopulation: `seed_superpop + 10000000 * variant`.
- New pathologists of the truth: `seed_superpop + 10000000 * variant + 1`.

**Output** (`simulation/data/`)

- `02_1_pathologist_variants.csv`: parameters of the variants.
- `02_1_pathologist_observed_data.csv.xz`: one row per slide, rater, dataset and variant: `scenario`,
  `n_slide`, `rep`, `seed`, `variant`, `slide`, `rater_ID`, `P`, `TP`, `FN`, `FP`.
- `02_1_truth_average_pathologist.csv`: `scenario`, `variant`, `name`, `averaging`, `truth`.
- `02_1_truth_new_pathologists.csv.xz`: `scenario`, `variant`, `pathologist`, `name`, `averaging`,
  `truth`.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
```

# Functions
```{r}
# F1-score = harmonic mean of precision and recall (as in the example Rmds).
# Returns 0 if precision or recall is 0 (paper "Case B").
calc_F1_score <- function(Precision, Recall) {
  case_when(
    Precision == 0 ~ 0, # Set F1-Score to 0 if Precision is 0
    Recall == 0 ~ 0, # Set F1-Score to 0 if Recall is 0
    T ~ 2 * (Precision*Recall / (Precision + Recall)) # Normal F1-Score
  )
}

# Slide effects on logit recall and log FP_rate, correlated normals (Cholesky, as in step 2)
draw_slide_effects <- function(slides, sd_slide_difficulty_recall, sd_slide_difficulty_FPrate,
                               cor_slide_difficulty) {
  slides |>
    mutate(
      z_recall       = rnorm(n()),
      z_FP_rate      = rnorm(n()),
      effect_recall  = sd_slide_difficulty_recall * z_recall,
      effect_FP_rate = sd_slide_difficulty_FPrate *
        (cor_slide_difficulty * z_recall + sqrt(1 - cor_slide_difficulty^2) * z_FP_rate)
    ) |>
    select(-z_recall, -z_FP_rate)
}

# True recall and expected FP of each cell (slide x rater) from the slide effects and the
# rater's skill and cutoff
add_cell_values <- function(df, recall, FP_rate, fp_per_object, rater_FP_scale) {
  df |>
    mutate(
      recall_slide      = plogis(qlogis(recall) + effect_recall + skill + cutoff),
      FP_expected_slide = FP_rate * exp(effect_FP_rate + rater_FP_scale * (cutoff - skill)) +
        fp_per_object * P
    )
}

# One pathologist dataset: every rater scores every slide (one row per slide x rater)
simulate_rater_dataset <- function(
    slides, # Slide dataset with ground truth object counts
    n_rater, # Number of raters (pathologists)
    recall, FP_rate, # Performance of the median rater
    fp_per_object, # FP per true object
    sd_slide_difficulty_recall, sd_slide_difficulty_FPrate, cor_slide_difficulty, # Slide effects
    sd_rater_skill, sd_rater_cutoff, rater_FP_scale # Rater effects
    ) {
  df_slides <- draw_slide_effects(slides, sd_slide_difficulty_recall, sd_slide_difficulty_FPrate,
                                  cor_slide_difficulty)
  df_raters <- tibble(
    rater_ID = seq_len(n_rater),
    skill    = rnorm(n_rater, 0, sd_rater_skill),
    cutoff   = rnorm(n_rater, 0, sd_rater_cutoff)
  )

  cross_join(df_slides, df_raters) |>
    add_cell_values(recall, FP_rate, fp_per_object, rater_FP_scale) |>
    mutate(
      TP = rbinom(n(), P, recall_slide),
      FN = P - TP,
      FP = rpois(n(), FP_expected_slide)
    ) |>
    select(slide, rater_ID, P, TP, FN, FP)
}

# Marginal truth from per-rater sums of the expected counts and per-rater grouped values
# (formulas as calc_true_metrics() in step 2):
#   pooled  = metric of the summed expected counts (over the raters of the group)
#   grouped = mean of the per-cell metrics (every rater has the same slides, so the mean of the
#             per-rater grouped values = mean over the cells)
calc_marginal_truth <- function(df) {
  df |>
    summarise(
      Recall_pooled    = sum(TP_sum) / sum(P_sum),
      Precision_pooled = sum(TP_sum) / sum(TP_sum + FP_sum),
      F1_pooled        = 2 * sum(TP_sum) / sum(P_sum + TP_sum + FP_sum),
      across(ends_with("_grouped"), mean)
    ) |>
    pivot_longer(matches("_(pooled|grouped)$"),
                 names_to = c("name", "averaging"), names_sep = "_", values_to = "truth")
}
```

# Settings
```{r}
offset_pathologists <- 10000000 # seed offset of this step
n_new_pathologists  <- 20000    # new raters for the truths
n_truth_slides      <- 10000    # superpopulation slides for the truths
reps                <- 1:100
```

# Load slides
```{r}
# Pathologist design: scenarios A-C (scenario D of step 1 is only used in the ML design)
df_slide_scenarios <- read_csv("simulation/data/01_slide_scenarios.csv") |>
  filter(scenario %in% c("A", "B", "C"))
df_slides          <- read_csv("simulation/data/01_slides.csv.xz") |>
  filter(scenario %in% c("A", "B", "C"), n_slide == 40, rep %in% reps)
df_slides_superpop <- read_csv("simulation/data/01_slides_superpop.csv.xz") |>
  filter(scenario %in% c("A", "B", "C"))
```

# Pathologist variants
```{r}
df_variants <- tribble(
  ~variant, ~variant_name,     ~n_rater, ~recall, ~FP_rate, ~fp_per_object, ~sd_slide_difficulty_recall, ~sd_slide_difficulty_FPrate, ~cor_slide_difficulty, ~sd_rater_skill, ~sd_rater_cutoff, ~rater_FP_scale,
  1,        "data example",    23,       0.63,    4.2,      0.015,          0.66,                        0.95,                        0,                     0.20,            0.55,             2.0,
  2,        "skilled panel",   9,        0.70,    3.0,      0.015,          0.66,                        0.95,                        0,                     0.55,            0.20,             2.0
)

df_variants
```

# Generate counts
```{r}
# One simulation per dataset and variant, each with its own seed
df_sim <- df_slides |>
  nest(slides = c(slide, group, P)) |>
  cross_join(df_variants) |>
  mutate(
    seed_counts = seed + offset_pathologists * variant,
    sim = pmap(pick(slides, seed_counts, n_rater:rater_FP_scale), \(slides, seed_counts, ...) {
      set.seed(seed_counts)
      simulate_rater_dataset(slides, ...)
    })
  ) |>
  select(scenario, n_slide, rep, seed, variant, sim)

# Counts (without the rater effects)
df_counts <- df_sim |>
  unnest(sim) |>
  select(scenario, n_slide, rep, seed, variant, slide, rater_ID, P, TP, FN, FP)
```

# Truths
```{r}
# Superpopulation slides with own slide effects per scenario and variant
df_truth_slides <- df_slides_superpop |>
  nest(slides = c(slide, group, P)) |>
  left_join(distinct(df_slide_scenarios, scenario, seed_superpop), by = "scenario") |>
  cross_join(df_variants) |>
  mutate(
    seed_slides = seed_superpop + offset_pathologists * variant,
    slides = pmap(pick(slides, seed_slides, sd_slide_difficulty_recall:cor_slide_difficulty),
                  \(slides, seed_slides, ...) {
                    set.seed(seed_slides)
                    draw_slide_effects(slides, ...)
                  })
  )

# Per rater: n_new_pathologists new raters x the first n_truth_slides superpopulation slides,
# one scenario and variant at a time (only the per-rater summaries are kept)
df_truth_raters <- df_truth_slides |>
  mutate(raters = pmap(pick(slides, seed_slides, recall, FP_rate, fp_per_object,
                            sd_rater_skill, sd_rater_cutoff, rater_FP_scale),
                       \(slides, seed_slides, recall, FP_rate, fp_per_object,
                         sd_rater_skill, sd_rater_cutoff, rater_FP_scale) {
                         set.seed(seed_slides + 1)
                         tibble(pathologist = seq_len(n_new_pathologists),
                                skill       = rnorm(n_new_pathologists, 0, sd_rater_skill),
                                cutoff      = rnorm(n_new_pathologists, 0, sd_rater_cutoff)) |>
                           cross_join(slides |> filter(slide <= n_truth_slides)) |>
                           add_cell_values(recall, FP_rate, fp_per_object, rater_FP_scale) |>
                           mutate(TP_expected = P * recall_slide) |>
                           group_by(pathologist) |>
                           summarise(
                             Recall_grouped    = mean(recall_slide),
                             Precision_grouped = mean(TP_expected / (TP_expected + FP_expected_slide)),
                             F1_grouped        = mean(2 * TP_expected / (P + TP_expected + FP_expected_slide)),
                             TP_sum = sum(TP_expected), P_sum = sum(P), FP_sum = sum(FP_expected_slide)
                           )
                       })) |>
  select(scenario, variant, raters)

# Average pathologist: over all raters (same raters and slides as the single pathologists)
df_truth_average <- df_truth_raters |>
  mutate(truth = map(raters, calc_marginal_truth)) |>
  select(scenario, variant, truth) |>
  unnest(truth)

# Single pathologist: per rater
df_truth_new <- df_truth_raters |>
  mutate(truth = map(raters, \(raters) raters |> group_by(pathologist) |> calc_marginal_truth() |> ungroup())) |>
  select(scenario, variant, truth) |>
  unnest(truth)
```

# Save
```{r}
write_csv(df_variants, "simulation/data/02_1_pathologist_variants.csv")
write_csv(df_counts, "simulation/data/02_1_pathologist_observed_data.csv.xz")
write_csv(df_truth_average, "simulation/data/02_1_truth_average_pathologist.csv")
write_csv(df_truth_new, "simulation/data/02_1_truth_new_pathologists.csv.xz")
```

# Check
```{r}
# Number of datasets and raters per scenario and variant
df_counts |>
  group_by(scenario, n_slide, variant) |>
  summarise(datasets = n_distinct(rep), raters_per_dataset = n_distinct(rater_ID),
            rows = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Monte Carlo SE of the average pathologist: bootstrap over the raters (2000 resamples)
set.seed(1)
df_mc_se <- df_truth_raters |>
  mutate(mc_se = map(raters, \(raters)
    map(1:2000, \(b) raters |> slice_sample(prop = 1, replace = TRUE) |> calc_marginal_truth()) |>
      bind_rows() |>
      group_by(name, averaging) |>
      summarise(mc_se = sd(truth), .groups = "drop"))) |>
  select(scenario, variant, mc_se) |>
  unnest(mc_se)

# Average pathologist (with its Monte Carlo SE) vs. distribution of the single pathologists
# (median and central 95 %)
df_truth_new |>
  group_by(scenario, variant, name, averaging) |>
  summarise(new_q025 = quantile(truth, 0.025), new_median = median(truth),
            new_mean = mean(truth), new_q975 = quantile(truth, 0.975), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(df_truth_average |> rename(average = truth), by = c("scenario", "variant", "name", "averaging")) |>
  left_join(df_mc_se, by = c("scenario", "variant", "name", "averaging")) |>
  arrange(averaging, variant, name, scenario)
```
